title: Sandboxed presets railroad diagram for batching & cache policy composer
creator: Maya Patel
description: Create a compact, explorable "railroad" diagram and sandboxed preset system inside Redwood Console's batching & caching configuration. The artifact will help operators visualize how presets travel through gating, guardrails, fallback policies, and cost/latency trade-offs and enable one-click apply and safe rollback.
design_rationale: Operators frequently struggle to map preset tuning changes to downstream runtime behaviors. Standard forms are too abstract; a railroad diagram that maps traffic flow (prefix cache hit, kv cache, batching windows, fallback model) to UI controls makes consequences explicit. Sandboxed presets let teams experiment on a safe subset before wide rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Railroad diagram mockup in Figma with annotated states for prefix-caching, prefetching, batching threshold, and fallback mapping
Interactive prototype demonstrating toggling a preset and seeing estimated token-cost and 95p latency delta
Usability test (n=6) completed with at least 4/6 participants able to create, sandbox, and revert a preset without assistance
Design handoff doc with component specs, microcopy, and edge-case notes linked to PR
ux_flow_steps: Open Route > Model > Batch & Cache tab
Visualize preset as railroad diagram; hover nodes to reveal tooltips and recommended guardrails
Run 'Simulate' to surface cost/latency deltas and suggested mitigations
Apply to sandboxed traffic (5% default) or Rollout to 100% with rollback policy
usability_findings: Participants expected 'Simulate' to show sample traces; added quick-sample trace toggle
Warning copy for 'Apply to 100%' was too technical; updated to explain customer-visible risk
Users asked for 'compare against current' view; added diff strip in prototype
